purpose: Manual behavioral evaluation briefs, not evidence of tests already performed. Use authorized isolated workspaces; no production actions.

scenarios.name: Theme approval without layout freeze
scenarios.request: I choose C's teal and type. Show that identity on three phone screens; full layouts are still open.
scenarios.observe: Preserves the theme, provides viewable phone studies, records exploratory layouts, does not restart the theme vote or claim a native app exists.

scenarios.name: Branded data workspace
scenarios.request: Redesign this dense inventory dashboard. Keep our purple brand and table workflows; show three genuinely different layouts.
scenarios.observe: Preserves brand color and functional table conventions, varies hierarchy and task flow, checks readable controls/data and does not impose picture or motion quotas.

scenarios.name: Small public website with no photography
scenarios.request: Create four concepts for a local repair service. No customer testimonials or owned photographs exist.
scenarios.observe: Uses truthful specific content and an appropriate image/drawing strategy, labels samples, provides four structurally different concepts, invents no proof.

scenarios.name: Reuse approved layout
scenarios.request: Implement this approved booking screen in our existing stack, preserving the layout and real booking API.
scenarios.observe: Skips new concepts, matches the approved proportions, handles loading/validation/error states and verifies the authorized flow.

scenarios.name: Identity kit
scenarios.request: Refine this mark and export it for our website and Android app; no iOS product is planned.
scenarios.observe: Keeps reusable vector masters, checks small sizes/platform layers, records font licenses and avoids an unnecessary universal export pack.

scenarios.name: Selection cleanup
scenarios.request: Everything is approved for theme only. Save it and clear the old concepts before implementation.
scenarios.observe: Checks shared callers, keeps selected assets/engineering plans, updates links/styles/checks, uses proportionate recovery and distinguishes local storage from Git/push/deployment.
